newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission plans to cut excess olive oil cost.
newsitem.headline: Commission plans to cut excess olive oil cost.

text.p: The cost implications of large anticipated over-production of olive oil are behind the European Commission's plans to reform the sector, according to a Commission document obtained by Reuters.
The document drawn up by farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is due to be put to the Commission for adoption on February 12.
The plans emphasize the need to promote quality, end fraud and limit the cost of support.

While maintaining the present import-export regime as a tool for managing prices, the Commission suggests that a study should be made of proposals to move away from export refunds towards promoting overseas sales for prime quality oil.

Foreseeing considerable overproduction in the future the Commission suggests that the introduction of national guaranteed quantities, along the lines of milk quotas in the dairy sector, could appeal to member states who want to guarantee support for the sector at national level.
"The advantages amount to the defence of the status quo in each member state and a certain guarantee for producers as has been experienced, for example, in the dairy sector," the report says.
Consumption aid would be increased and the Commission adds that by returning the aid to former levels control mechanisms would be reinforced.

"With the aid at its present level of 12 ecus per 100 kg, the serious perpetrator of fraud against the consumer may find it worth his while to simply opt out of the consumption aid system and avoid controls associated with it," the document says.

Commissioner Fischler has said that the olive oil sector is among the worst for fraud and the report blames the fact that small producers who draw one type of aid then sell on to large crushers and distributors who also claim aid.

The report says that under its proposals the two different forms of production aid (flat rate and real) would be abolished to be replaced by an aid per tree paid on demand and subject to conditions enforced by member states.
Public intervention and so-called 'buffer stock storage' would be abolished to be replaced by a system of private storage and olive trees would be checked by satellite.
With the introduction of tree aid the current system of co- financing olive oil control agencies would be phased out.
